_README: FROZEN-COUNT BASELINE for scripts/check-design-tokens.ts (Tier 2).
WHAT THIS FILE IS
The number of design.md conformance violations that existed in apps/web when
the conformance gate was introduced, for the two codes whose remediation is
too large to land in one change. Every entry is known, itemised, standing
design debt with a number attached — not permitted drift.
THE ONLY RULE: THESE NUMBERS MAY ONLY EVER GO DOWN.
The check fails if any count rises above its baseline, and names exactly which
classes grew and by how much. A brand-new class has an implicit baseline of 0,
so introducing one fails immediately. RAISING A NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS NEVER
THE FIX — `--write-baseline` refuses to do it. Remove the new violations.
WHEN YOU REMOVE VIOLATIONS
Lower the baseline IN THE SAME COMMIT, or the ground you gained is not held
and someone can silently spend it again. The check prints the delta on every
run, including decreases, so a stale-high number cannot hide. Regenerate with:
pnpm tsx scripts/check-design-tokens.ts --write-baseline
WHEN A CLASS REACHES ZERO
The check tells you when a Tailwind ramp stop has reached zero usage and can
be banned outright in .eslintrc.js's no-restricted-syntax rule. Add it there;
that converts frozen debt into a permanently closed door.
WHY THESE TWO CODES AND NOTHING ELSE
ALIAS_SPELLING and DERIVED_RAMP are ~1,125 mechanical spelling swaps across 82
files (`text-neutral-500` -> `text-ash`, `text-neutral-300` -> `text-pewter`,
and so on). Every other code is Tier 1 and blocks the build on any occurrence,
including the four document-level consistency checks, which are at zero and
must stay there. Do not add a code here to make a build pass.
Recorded 2026-07-24 against design.md's 14 canonical tokens.
